title: Workspace Heartbeat MCP Plugin v1
goal: Build and validate a minimal MCP heartbeat tool plus ChatGPT conversation-panel UI so long-running workspace-control tasks can publish natural-language progress through a real tool call into one continuously updating side panel.
acceptance_criteria: Expose a model-callable heartbeat_update tool whose user-facing progress content is natural prose rather than rigid structured headings.
Expose a read-only heartbeat_get tool that returns the latest heartbeat plus bounded history for an optional task ID.

Use task_id as the stable heartbeat identity across ChatGPT model/app session differences and chat handoffs; session metadata may resolve omitted task IDs but must not partition authoritative task progress.
Advertise a ChatGPT thread conversation-panel entrypoint that renders beside a normal Chat conversation.
Keep the last known valid heartbeat visible until a newer heartbeat arrives; empty/failed polls must never erase valid progress or force a false IDLE state.
Render a bounded chronological log of prior heartbeat updates in the same panel, newest update last.
Assign monotonically increasing sequence numbers per task while the server process is alive and tolerate sequence restart after server restart through timestamp-based UI merge semantics.
Keep heartbeat state and history in memory only for this iteration; do not add a database or durable telemetry sink.
Require Node.js 20 or newer and fail dependency/runtime setup clearly on older runtimes.
Log successful MCP requests with method, status, and latency so live transport can be observed directly.
Keep the tools useful without UI through normal structuredContent/content results.
Do not mutate research-engine or any course/research repository as part of this plugin implementation.
constraints: Use current documented OpenAI/MCP Apps APIs and a ChatGPT thread entrypoint; do not depend on hidden client behavior.
Do not treat transient ChatGPT commentary/thought rendering as authoritative heartbeat delivery.
Do not expose private chain-of-thought; heartbeat_update carries concise operator-facing progress prose only.
Do not commit per-heartbeat runtime state to Git.
Do not add OAuth, a database, cloud hosting, durable history, or SSE/event streaming until the stable polling/history loop is proven.

Do not claim this MCP server can physically block unrelated GitHub or other external tool calls; the three-tool lease remains an executor contract unless operations are later proxied through a controllable orchestrator.
Do not automatically reset the panel to IDLE on assistant-response start because the current MCP App surface does not provide a reliable response-start lifecycle event.
Keep all implementation inside workspace-control plugins/workspace-heartbeat/** plus this task capsule/handoff.

notes: The user explicitly wants heartbeat delivery to be a tool call and the UI to be one updating formatted box, while heartbeat prose remains natural and conversational. Live evidence now proves the thread side panel renders in normal Chat mode. The first authorization attempt using 'Use once' produced an 'Unable to load conversation' error; retrying after refresh with 'Always allow' allowed the chat to continue. The research chat claimed the live heartbeat panel was working before the user had observed any panel; such model prose is not accepted as evidence. The MCP server currently logs startup/errors only, not successful requests, so an idle MCP terminal cannot prove that no request occurred. System Node v12.22.9 is unsupported for this implementation; Node 20 in a dedicated conda environment is the working runtime. tmux helpers heartbeat-up/heartbeat-status/heartbeat-console/heartbeat-down keep both MCP and ngrok alive across SSH disconnects. New live evidence proved transport and rendering but exposed a session-correlation defect: the panel sometimes polled heartbeat_get under a different or missing ChatGPT session identity, received no task, switched to IDLE, and later resurrected the prior heartbeat. The v0.2 correction makes task_id authoritative, retains bounded task history, persists active task/history in widget state, ignores empty polls after valid state, declares Node >=20, and logs successful MCP requests. The user's preferred UX is a sequential heartbeat log that does not disappear between updates. Automatic reset to IDLE on assistant-response start is intentionally deferred because no reliable response-start lifecycle signal is available. The panel-stability correction is repository-valid and canonical at 3214ec2be4f0c20933784b3d265386d9652dfd0b. The task is now blocked only on the user's live Lambda/ChatGPT smoke.
